title: Cross-Workspace Role Matrix + Access Timeline — prototype for audit-led RBAC review
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a console-first flow that helps admins and auditors understand who has access across multiple workspaces/orgs and why, by combining a cross-workspace role matrix with a time-based access timeline. The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence for audits, make role inheritance and exceptions visible, and provide action paths (revoke/grant/ask) directly from the audit surface.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates a cross-workspace role matrix with filters for role, permission, workspace, and user
Timeline view shows grant/revoke/change events over a selectable date range with link-to-log-event for each item
Action affordances (revoke/grant/request-approval) are discoverable and wired to mock API endpoints
Design includes mobile/responsive variants for the console's admin panel
Accessibility: contrast and keyboard nav documented; screen-reader labels for timeline events
design_notes: Primary problem: current console forces jumping between workspace pages and audit log to reconcile who had what access at a point in time
We propose a two-pane interface: left = role matrix (users x roles x workspaces aggregated), right = time-based event stream filtered by selected cell or user
Matrix should support aggregation rollups (org-level, folder-level, workspace-level) and show derived roles from group membership
Timeline items should include event type, actor, justification (if present), and link to raw audit log entry for compliance teams
Add on-hover micro-summaries that explain why a user has a role (direct grant vs group membership vs inherited)
Edge case: service accounts and token-scoped access — display with distinct iconography and non-interactive revoke paths (requires ENG workflow)
feedback_summary: PM (Arjun Patel): prioritise quick filters for compliance auditors — date range presets and CSV export are must-haves
Engineering (Sofia Alvarez): timeline must page results and support server-side filtering; agree to mock endpoints for prototype but production will need API gating
Security (Noah Li): require KMS audit-traceability for any revoke/grant action; flag 'security_review_required' true
Design review (Evelyn Park): prefer a condensed matrix row mode for large orgs; propose a sparklines column to show recent activity per user
UX Research (Daniela Ruiz): suggested 6 moderated sessions with enterprise admins; target metrics: time-to-answer and perceived trustworthiness
decisions: Ship prototype with server-side pagination for timeline and CSV export for matrix
Include a readonly badge for service accounts and tokens; revoke action disabled with tooltip linking to runbook
Prioritise role-inheritance microcopy to reduce false positives during audits
Defer role-edit flows to a separate ticket; this prototype focuses on visibility and remediation requests
next_steps: Share prototypes with ENG-identity and security for API contract alignment by 2025-11-14
Schedule 6 usability sessions (3 enterprise, 3 mid-market) in 2025-11-17 to 2025-11-24
Add CSV export acceptance test and create PM/ENG tickets for server-side pagination
Prepare accessibility checklist and run contrast & keyboard tests before design handoff
